purpose: Posaconazole is used to prevent and treat serious fungal infections, especially in people whose immune systems are weakened, such as those going through chemotherapy or organ transplants. It can fight infections caused by molds and yeasts that other antifungals may not cover well. Your doctor may also use it to treat certain stubborn fungal infections that have not responded to other treatments.
how_it_works: Posaconazole works by blocking a key substance that fungi need to build their protective outer wall, called the cell membrane. Without this wall, the fungus cannot survive or spread. Think of it like pulling out a critical building block so the fungus falls apart and cannot grow anymore.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach upset, headache, and fever. Some people also notice changes in their liver blood test results, which is why your doctor will check your blood periodically. Feeling tired or having a low potassium level can also happen.
warnings: This medication can affect your liver, so tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness. Posaconazole can interact with many other medications and raise or lower their levels in your blood, so always give your doctor and pharmacist a full list of everything you take. It may also affect your heart rhythm, so let your doctor know if you have any heart conditions. Avoid it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on what you are being treated for and which form you are taking — tablet, liquid suspension, or IV. A common adult dose for prevention of fungal infections is one 300 mg delayed-release tablet twice on the first day, then 300 mg once daily after that. The liquid suspension is usually taken with a full meal to help your body absorb it properly. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
